Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Grand Junction CO
1051 PM MST Fri Nov 13 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Valley rain and mountain snow returns to the forecast this 
  weekend favoring the southern mountains and adjacent 
  foothills.

- Quiet conditions return briefly Sunday afternoon and Monday
  before another round of precipitation arrives during the
  middle of next week.

- Unsettled and cool conditions are favored to persist into the
  late week period as well. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1050 PM MST Fri Nov 13 2026

The H500 hand analysis map this evening is playing out as
expected with an Omega-like pattern in place. A strong 
downstream blocking trough over eastern NOAM is forcing the 
upstream trough to negatively tilt as it moves farther inland. 
In between the highly amplified ridge remains but has shifted 
onto the Plains from 24 hours ago. Showers have developed in the
western CWA and with a strong PV lobe rotating across the 4 
Corners overnight...a few strikes of lightning will be possible.
Weaker echos on the radar suggest moisture is increasing on the
southerly flow into the southern mountains but so far webcams 
and snotels are relatively quiet. This will be changing in the 
next few hours with the heaviest precipitation still expected 
during the early to mid morning hours on Saturday as the surface
front and large scale coincide with moisture in place. Snow 
levels still look to hover in the 8-9kft level for the bulk of 
this event...lowering to mountain bases by sunset tomorrow as 
the system is exiting. The southern mountains...especially the 
crescent of the southern San Juans remain favored to catch the 
best moisture and produce the highest snow amounts. 4 to 8 
inches should cover most of the advisory area though hi-res 
guidance is picking out some of the favored high peaks and 
snotels for the higher amounts closer to a foot. Otherwise 1 to 
4 inches should cover the remaining mountain forecasts though 
colder northwest flow often throws some bonus inches. QPF 
amounts in the southern basins are still in the 1/3 to 2/3 inch 
range for liquid precipitation with again some isolated higher 
amounts possible due to the convection. Hydrographs are still 
only showing some minor rises on the smaller tributaries to the 
San Juan with the main steam holding steady. Temperatures will 
be much cooler tomorrow in the post frontal environment but 
overall end up near to above normal in the drier northern CWA 
and 5 to 10 degrees cooler in the wetter southern areas. By 
sunrise on Sunday the trough and PV stream will be east of the 
divide and ridging will be translate across the Great Basin to 
the Great Plains through Monday afternoon as the next deep 
trough arrives to the West. Models still show a moderate AR with
this system which again survives the upstream terrain and 
brings more widespread precipitation to the area in the mid week
time frame. The QG forcing has been trending a bit farther 
North which will bring better chances for precipitation to our 
northern CWA which as been missing out lately. This system is a 
tad cooler and this should translate to better a snowfall 
forecast for most of the higher terrain...but will need to 
continue to watch trends in speed and track as we get nearer. 
Temperatures will moderate to near normal Monday into Tuesday 
before a colder end to the week. Models spread still significant
and changing daily on how the pattern in the late week period 
evolves but the overall flavor is for a large trough in the West
keeping unsettled conditions on the radar. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SUNDAY/... 
Issued at 1050 PM MST Fri Nov 13 2026

Moisture is beginning to increase with scattered showers developing 
and lowering cigs over eastern Utah and southern Colorado. Expect 
precipitation coverage to increase with light rain showers in valley 
terminals with light snow showers mixing in for mountain sites. The 
precipitation and lowering cigs could lead to ILS breakpoints being 
reached after 06z. Precipitation is expected to decrease in coverage 
Saturday afternoon.

&&

.GJT WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...

CO...Winter Weather Advisory until 9 PM MST Saturday for COZ019.
UT...None.

&&
